set.body:
Phase D (architecture). ABSORBS P7.5 (bd-01KYNA5EPTP9Y8QAH1673G613D), which is strictly smaller: P7.5 covers the agent<->client wire string-stuffing and says nothing about the scheduler adapter's flattening or the cancellation law.

Problem: ssh/Slurm.scala:219-226 has no match at all —

    private def invocationFailure(failure: AgentFailure): F[InvocationResult] =
      failureEvidence(failure).map(evidence =>
        InvocationResult.SpawnFailed(SpawnFailureKind.Unknown, Diagnostics.one(...), evidence))

Every one of the 7 AgentFailure variants (protocol/AgentProtocol.scala:144-155) becomes the same SpawnFailed(Unknown). The only surviving distinction is a diagnostic STRING code from agentFailureCode (:253-261). The low-level SSH implementation has the distinctions; the scheduler adapter destroys them. observe/accounting/capabilities route through queryResult (:213-217) with the same flattening.

The target ADT is also richer than what is used: SpawnFailureKind (kernel/Contracts.scala:44-50) has ExecutableMissing, PermissionDenied, WorkingDirectoryMissing, EnvironmentInvalid, ResourceUnavailable — so AgentUnavailable never becomes ExecutableMissing, AuthenticationFailed never becomes PermissionDenied, and an SSH exchange timeout never becomes InvocationResult.TimedOut.

Semantic lie worth naming: "SpawnFailed" asserts the process never ran, which is FALSE for RemoteCliFailure, RemoteAgentFailure and ProtocolViolation — all of which arise AFTER a successful exchange (SshAgentWireClient.scala:103-126).

Also: a ProtocolViolation from a truncated response on a zero-exit ssh goes to InvocationFailed — a definite "not submitted" — even though AcceptanceUncertainty.ResponseUnparseable and ResponseLost exist (core/FailureModel.scala:13-14) and the CLI path uses them (SlurmCliScheduler.scala:56).

Fix: a generic CallFailure algebra, cleaner than squeezing protocol and transport failures into process-execution vocabulary. Public names remain a design choice.
set.title: P8.D5: CallFailure algebra preserved to the boundary
